chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، عَنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ الْوَشَّاءِ، عَنِ ابْنِ سِنَّانَ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Masud, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Ibn Sinan who said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ يَقُولُ: بَيْنَمَا أَنَا فِي الطَّوَافِ إِذَا رَجُلٌ يَجْذِبُ ثَوْبِي، فَالْتَفَتُّ فَإِذَا عِبَادٌ الْبَصْرِيُّ، قَالَ: يَا جَعْفَرَ بْنَ مُحَمَّدٍ تَلْبَسُ مِثْلَ هَذَا الثَّوْبِ وَأَنْتَ فِي الْمَوْضِعِ الَّذِي أَنْتَ فِيهِ مِنْ عَلِيٍّ صَلَوَاتُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ، قَالَ: قُلْتُ: وَيْلَكَ هَذَا ثَوْبُ قُوهِيَّ اشْتَرَيْتُهُ بِدِينَارٍ وَكَسْرٍ، وَكَانَ عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ فِي زَمَانٍ يَسْتَقِيمُ لَهُ مَا لَبِسَ فِيهِ، وَلَوْ لَبِسْتُ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ اللِّبَاسَ فِي زَمَانِنَا لَقَالَ النَّاسُ: هَذَا مِرَاءٌ مِثْلُ عِبَادٍ!

translations.en: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: While I was performing the Tawaf, a man started pulling my garment. I turned to look at him and found it was 'Abbad al-Basri. He said: O Ja'far ibn Muhammad, you wear this type of cloth while you are in the position you are in regarding Ali (peace be upon him). I said to him: Woe be upon you, this is a Quhai cloth that I bought for a Dinar and a fraction [of a Dirham]. Ali (peace be upon him) was in an era where what he wore was befitting, but if I were to wear that same attire in our time, the people would say: This is a show-off like 'Abbad!

en.summary: This hadith from Al-Kashi’s *Rijal* highlights the Imam’s nuanced understanding of *fiqh al-waqi'* (jurisprudence of context), illustrating how social perception (*mir'a'*) dictates the appropriateness of attire. It underscores the Shia scholarly principle that outward simplicity is not an absolute virtue but must be balanced against the risk of being mistaken for ostentation (*riya'*) in different historical eras. The incident serves as a practical example of the Imams' adaptability to the cultural and social norms of their time to preserve the dignity of the Ahl al-Bayt.
en.seo_question: Why did Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq wear simple clothes despite his status?

key_terms.قُوهِيَّ: Quhai (a type of cloth from Kuhistan)
